name: Understanding Quadrilaterals — Polygon Angle Sums and Properties
whatIsIt: Every POLYGON (a closed flat shape with straight sides) has an interior angle sum you can predict: (n − 2) × 180°, where n is the number of sides. A triangle (n=3) gives 180°; a quadrilateral (n=4) gives 360°; a pentagon (n=5) gives 540°. The EXTERIOR angles of any convex polygon always add up to 360°, no matter how many sides. Quadrilaterals also come in special families — PARALLELOGRAM (opposite sides parallel and equal), RHOMBUS (parallelogram with all 4 sides equal, diagonals cross at right angles), RECTANGLE (parallelogram with all angles 90°), KITE (two pairs of adjacent equal sides), and TRAPEZIUM (exactly one pair of parallel sides) — each with its own rules about sides, angles and diagonals.
whyNeeded: Architects and carpenters use the polygon angle-sum rule to cut roof panels, tile floors and build multi-sided frames without measuring every angle. Knowing which quadrilateral you have (rhombus, kite, trapezium...) tells you instantly which sides and angles are equal — a shortcut used in construction, design and craft.
realLifeUses: A pentagon-shaped stop-sign or hut roof — each interior angle is 108° because (5−2)×180 = 540, and 540÷5 = 108 for a regular pentagon
A kite (the toy) has two pairs of equal adjacent sides — that's literally why it's called a kite
A rhombus-patterned floor tile (like a cricket-pitch diamond) has diagonals that cross at exactly 90°
A trapezium-shaped table or bridge truss has only one pair of parallel sides

vocabulary.meaning: A closed flat shape made of straight sides (triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon...).
The total of all inside angles of a polygon: (n − 2) × 180°.
The angle between a side and the extension of the next side; all exterior angles of a convex polygon add to 360°.
A parallelogram with all 4 sides equal; diagonals cross at right angles and bisect each other.
A quadrilateral with two pairs of adjacent (touching) sides equal; one pair of opposite angles are equal.
A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides.

story.title: The Pentagon Garden Bed
story.text: Dada is building a five-sided (pentagon) garden bed and needs to know each corner angle to cut the wood right. 'Is there a rule?' asks Meera. 'Yes — for any polygon, angles add up to (n minus 2) times 180,' says Dada. 'A pentagon has 5 sides, so (5−2)×180 = 3×180 = 540°. If it's a REGULAR pentagon, all five angles are equal: 540 ÷ 5 = 108° each.' Meera measures — 108° it is, and the bed fits together perfectly.

standardMethod.summary: Use (n − 2) × 180° for a polygon's interior angle sum; divide by n for a REGULAR polygon's single angle. Exterior angles of any convex polygon always total 360°.
steps: Count the number of sides, n.
If the polygon is REGULAR (all sides and angles equal), divide the sum by n to get one angle.
Exterior angles always add up to 360° for any convex polygon, whatever n is.

alternateMethods.name: Diagonals-from-one-vertex trick
alternateMethods.whenToUse: To SEE why the (n−2)×180° formula is true, not just memorise it.
steps: Pick one vertex (corner) of the polygon.
Draw diagonals from it to every other non-adjacent vertex.
This splits the polygon into (n − 2) triangles.
Each triangle's angles sum to 180°, so the whole polygon sums to (n − 2) × 180°.
alternateMethods.example: A hexagon (n=6): drawing diagonals from one vertex makes 4 triangles, so its angle sum is 4 × 180° = 720°.

workedExamples.problem: What is the interior angle sum of a hexagon (6 sides)?
A quadrilateral has three angles of 90°, 85° and 95°. What is the fourth angle?
A rhombus has diagonals of length 6 cm and 8 cm. Since a rhombus's diagonals cross at right angles and bisect each other, what shape is formed by one quarter of it?
steps: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other AND cross at 90°.
Each half-diagonal is 3 cm and 4 cm.
One quarter of the rhombus is a right triangle with legs 3 cm and 4 cm.
workedExamples.answer: A right triangle with legs 3 cm and 4 cm

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting to subtract 2 from n before multiplying by 180° (e.g. using n × 180° instead of (n−2) × 180°).
commonMistakes.fix: Always subtract 2 FIRST: (n − 2) × 180°. For a pentagon that's (5−2)×180 = 540°, not 5×180 = 900°.

commonMistakes.mistake: Mixing up which quadrilateral has which property — e.g. saying every parallelogram has equal diagonals, or every kite is a rhombus.
commonMistakes.fix: Only a RECTANGLE (or square) has equal diagonals. Only a RHOMBUS (or square) has all 4 sides equal AND diagonals at 90°. A kite has two PAIRS of adjacent equal sides, not all four equal — check the specific rule for each shape.

commonMistakes.mistake: Thinking the exterior-angle-sum rule (360°) changes with the number of sides, like the interior rule does.
commonMistakes.fix: The sum of exterior angles is ALWAYS 360° for any convex polygon, no matter how many sides it has — only the interior sum grows with n.

revisionCard.summary: Interior angle sum of an n-sided polygon: (n−2) × 180°. Regular polygon: divide by n for one angle. Exterior angles of ANY convex polygon always total 360°. Rhombus: all sides equal, diagonals cross at 90°. Kite: two pairs of adjacent equal sides. Trapezium: exactly one pair of parallel sides. Parallelogram: opposite sides parallel & equal.

rememberIt.hook: Interior angle sum of a polygon: (n − 2) × 180°. Exterior angles: always 360° total.
rememberIt.unpack: Rhombus: all sides equal, diagonals at 90°. Kite: two pairs of adjacent equal sides. Trapezium: one pair of parallel sides. Parallelogram: opposite sides parallel & equal. Rectangle: parallelogram with all 90° angles.

studentQuestions.q: Why does a triangle's angle sum equal 180° in the polygon formula?
studentQuestions.a: For n=3: (3−2)×180° = 1×180° = 180° — the formula matches the familiar triangle rule exactly, since a triangle can't be split into any smaller triangles from one vertex.

studentQuestions.q: What's the difference between a rhombus and a kite?
studentQuestions.a: A rhombus has all FOUR sides equal. A kite has two PAIRS of adjacent (touching) sides equal, but the two pairs can be different lengths from each other.
